title: Component subroutine: merging algorithm correctness only sketched (completeness lemma missing)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Severity: critical.**

Theorem 3's algorithm and its correctness are given only as a one-sentence sketch in Section 4.1: the procedure "maintains a family of vertex-disjoint directed paths covering $V(D)$ and repeatedly applies the Merge Lemma ... whenever the local configuration of an out-branching rooted at $s$ (resp. in-branching at $t$) permits it; correctness rests on the fact that two branches sharing only their common root and joined by an arc between their far endpoints can always be merged." This is a sketch, not a proof. Unspecified/unproved:

1. **Algorithm specification.** Which two paths are merged at each step and under exactly what condition; the stopping rule; how the out-/in-branching is used. (Should be an explicit algorithm box.)
2. **Completeness (hard direction).** Why, when no further merge is available, a single-path family is *equivalent* to existence of a Hamiltonian $(s,t)$-path. A greedy merge can get stuck; BGH-type correctness requires a structural lemma that in a strongly connected (or augmented) path-mergeable digraph a maximal *un-mergeable* path family covering all vertices must already be a single path. This lemma is absent.
3. **Finding-whenever-exists.** The "$\le n-1$ merges" bound only counts successful merges; it does not show the algorithm outputs a Hamiltonian path whenever one exists.

The Merge Lemma (Lemma 1) is correctly proved and is the right engine, but the completeness lemma — the substantive part — is missing.
